children: has returned to the support line of Bitcoin’s Power Law, says Fidelity Investments’ Jurrien Timmer. A fall well below that line, now near $62,000 and rising, would challenge his entire model.
However, Timmer stays bullish, citing the four-year cycle. For BTC holders, the retest asks whether cycle-based models still work as global liquidity recedes.
What Is Bitcoin’s Power Law, and Why Does Its Support Line Matter?
Bitcoin’s Power Law plots price against time on a logarithmic chart. Fidelity’s version adds a trendline and a lower support line.
On Timmer’s chart, the 2015 low of $230 landed below the line’s $252 reading. In contrast, the 2018 trough of $3,204 held above its $2,521 mark.
“I remain bullish on Bitcoin based on its four-year cycle and Power Law math, but it’s a bit disheartening that we are back again sitting on that power law support curve.”
Jurrien Timmer, Director of Global Macro at Fidelity Investments.

The same note ties Bitcoin’s weakness to receding global liquidity and fading risk appetite as the AI theme corrects. Bitcoin has also moved more in step with the S&P 500 lately, which Timmer reads as speculative-asset behavior.
Veteran trader Peter Brandt shared the chart on X. Brandt has separately asked whether his own weekly chart shows a head-and-shoulders top, a formation that can precede a decline.
In contrast, James Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus, read that chart as a bullish inverse pattern. He said a drop below $57,000 would prove him wrong.
